title: The surgeon riddle
teaser: A father and son are in a car crash. The surgeon says, 'I can't operate. He's my son.' How? In a 2021 study, fewer than a third of students said the surgeon could be a woman.

slides.alt: Puzzle No. 02: A father and son are in a car crash. The father dies. At the hospital, the surgeon looks at the boy and says, 'I can't operate. He's my son.' How? Comment your answer before you swipe.
A hint: picture the surgeon. Who did you see? Read it again. Nothing in it says who the surgeon is.
The answer: his mum. The surgeon is the boy's mother. Also right: his other dad, in a family with two fathers.

How many get it: researchers gave the riddle to 152 US university students. 30% said the surgeon could be a woman. 36% said the surgeon could be a second father. Source: Belle and colleagues, 2021, Sex Roles.
Why your brain stalls: your brain fills the gap with a default picture, called a schema. The riddle only works because the right answer breaks that picture.
For teachers and designers: learners fill gaps with defaults too. When an example breaks the usual picture, say so out loud. Send this to someone and see who gets it first.

body: A father and son are in a car crash. The father dies. At the hospital, the surgeon looks at the boy and says, "I can't operate. He's my son." How?
The surgeon is his mother. (His other dad works too.)

In a 2021 study, researchers gave the riddle to 152 US university students. Fewer than a third (30%) said the surgeon could be a woman. More (36%) said the surgeon could be a second father in a same-sex marriage.
The riddle is hard because your brain fills the gap with its default picture of a surgeon, a schema, and the answer breaks it. Send this to someone and see who gets it first.
forDesigners: Learners fill gaps with defaults too. When an example breaks the usual picture, say so out loud.

sources.label: Belle, D., Tartarilla, A.B., Wapman, M. et al. (2021). "I can't operate, that boy is my son!": Gender schemas and a classic riddle. Sex Roles, 85, 161–171.
